metaDescription: Six portable carpet and upholstery spot cleaners at or under $150, including TREEUP steam, Uwant, MUJERBAY, Rosewill, HAPOW and Starrybot, compared honestly.
expertTake: The TREEUP portable steam cleaner is the pick at this cap because four modes, including a steam-only mode at 212 degrees, tackle greasy kitchen messes that cold-water spot cleaners cannot shift. The Starrybot with its 60 ounce clean tank is the value choice for pet stains on larger areas. Anyone cleaning whole rooms of wall-to-wall carpet should skip portable spot cleaners and use an upright deep cleaner.
introParagraphs: A portable carpet and upholstery cleaner is a spot tool: it sprays cleaning solution, scrubs with a small brush and sucks the dirty water back into a tank. It is built for stairs, couches, car seats and pet accidents, and it does that job far better than a rented machine hauled out once a year.

Prices move, and the $150 cap used here reflects live listing prices when this guide was updated. At this cap the real differences are tank capacity, hose reach, whether the machine heats its water and how much suction it really delivers, so the guide compares those rather than the biggest number on the box.

products.name: TREEUP Portable Steam Carpet Cleaner with 212F Steam and Hot Water Modes
products.description:
The TREEUP goes beyond a cold-water spot cleaner by adding steam and hot water modes. The steam-only setting reaches 212 degrees Fahrenheit and is aimed at greasy kitchen messes, while the other modes handle everyday stains. An 18 KPa suction claim and a 3.5 inch hand brush complete a fully equipped kit.

Heat is the real difference at this cap, since hot water loosens grease and dried-on food far better than cold. Against the Uwant steam model, it offers four modes where the Uwant offers three, but both share the 18 KPa label. Next to the MUJERBAY, it can reach a higher temperature in steam mode, though that mode uses water quickly and calls for care on delicate fabrics.

Test hot modes on a hidden patch first, since heat can set certain stains such as blood or dye. Rinse the tanks after every session and dry the brush. Descale if the steam output weakens, and keep the machine away from hardwood where steam can lift finishes. Blot fresh spills with a dry cloth before extracting, because a machine works best on the residue left behind rather than a puddle. On greasy spots, a short dwell time of five minutes with the solution before steaming lets the heat do the lifting instead of just spreading the grease around.
products.bestFor: Greasy kitchen and dining-room messes where hot water helps.
cons: Steam mode drains the tank quickly

products.name: Starrybot 18 KPa Pet Stain Extractor with 60 oz Clean Tank

specList.label: Tools
specList.value: 3 inch hand tool, 5 inch wide tool

products.description:
The Starrybot pairs an 18 KPa suction claim with the largest clean tank in this lineup at 60 ounces, plus a 40 ounce dirty tank. A 3 inch hand tool is meant for stubborn spots and a 5 inch wide tool for larger areas. The listing targets pet stains on carpets, sofas and car interiors.

A big clean tank means fewer trips to the sink, which matters when you are cleaning a staircase one step at a time. Set beside the Rosewill, its clean tank is larger but its dirty tank is smaller, so you may empty the dirty tank more often on heavily soiled jobs. Measured against the HAPOW, it has a bigger clean tank but a shorter documented cord and hose.

Empty the dirty tank before it nears full, because overfilling lets water reach the motor filter. Rinse the tanks and brushes after each session. Use a cleaning solution made for extractors, since ordinary detergents foam and clog the machine.
products.bestFor: Pet owners who need fewer refills on larger cleanups.
pros: 60 oz clean tank is the largest here

products.name: HAPOW 18 KPa Portable Carpet and Upholstery Cleaner, 13 ft Cord
products.description:
The HAPOW lists a 13.1 foot cord, a 4.9 foot hose and tanks of 1.8 liters clean and 0.9 liters dirty. The long cord and hose let you reach across a car interior or up a staircase without moving the base much. The listing claims 18 KPa suction and positions the machine for rugs, stair carpet, sofas and mattresses.

Reach is the practical advantage, since a short cord forces you to hunt for outlets and a short hose makes you drag the base up each step. Against the Starrybot, it has a longer documented cord and hose but a smaller clean tank. Next to the TREEUP, it offers no heating, so it suits fresh stains and not baked-on grease.

Check the hose connections for a firm seal, since a leak reduces suction. Rinse the tanks after use, and dry the brush head. Use the machine on a mattress sparingly, as too much water takes a long time to dry.
products.bestFor: Stairs, cars and mattresses where cord and hose reach matter.

products.name: Rosewill 550W 17 KPa Multi-Purpose Carpet and Upholstery Spot Cleaner
products.description:
The Rosewill states a 550W motor and 17 KPa suction, along with a 49 ounce clean tank and a larger 53.6 ounce dirty tank. Stating motor wattage is helpful, because it gives you something concrete to compare with other portable cleaners. The larger dirty tank is a thoughtful layout since the dirty tank fills faster than the clean one empties.

Set beside the Starrybot, its clean tank is smaller but its dirty tank is bigger, which suits heavily soiled jobs. Set beside the HAPOW, it lists motor wattage but no cord and hose length. Its suction claim is slightly lower than the 18 KPa units, but suction numbers from different brands are not directly comparable.

Empty the dirty tank after each job and rinse it thoroughly. Check the motor filter regularly and clean it. Store the machine with the tanks open to prevent odor. Because the motor is stated at 550W, it draws noticeable power, so plug it into a wall outlet rather than a thin extension cord. For upholstery, work from the top down in overlapping strokes and let each pass finish before moving on, which keeps the water from soaking the cushion core.
products.bestFor: Heavily soiled jobs where the dirty tank fills first.
pros: Larger dirty tank than clean tank
cons: Lower suction claim than 18 KPa units
Cord and hose length not listed

products.name: MUJERBAY UltraHeat Portable Spot and Stain Cleaner with Wheels
products.description:
The MUJERBAY UltraHeat heats the cleaning solution to 140 degrees Fahrenheit in under 15 seconds, which lifts and loosens tough stains better than cold water. Universal wheels and a handle make it easier to move around a room. The listing emphasizes localized cleaning that conserves water.

Heat to 140 degrees is a moderate level, safer for fabrics than a 212 degree steam mode while still helping with grease. Measured against the TREEUP, it gives up the steam mode but is gentler on delicate surfaces. Against the cold-water machines, it adds heat at a similar price.

Pick it if you want some heat without steam. Rinse the tanks after each session, and test on a hidden spot first. Wipe the wheels so grit does not scratch hard floors. A moderate temperature is a sensible compromise for most households, because most fabric care labels warn against high heat but allow warm water. Because the heater runs from a small tank, expect it to cycle on and off during a long session, and give it a minute between jobs so the water returns to temperature.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want moderate heat and a wheeled body.

products.name: Uwant 18 KPa Carpet Cleaner with Steam, Hot and Cold Water Modes
products.description:
The Uwant offers three cleaning modes, steam at 212 degrees Fahrenheit, hot water and cold water, with an 18 KPa suction claim and a multi-tool upholstery set. The maker's Pet Pro cleaning solution is formulated for pet messes. Three modes let you match heat to the fabric and the stain.

Measured against the TREEUP, it has one fewer mode but a similar steam capability, and the Pet Pro solution is a specific selling point for pet households. Next to the MUJERBAY, it offers a higher steam temperature. As with any steam machine, check the care label before using steam on delicate fabrics.

Use cold water on dye-prone fabrics, hot water on greasy stains and steam only on tough spots. Rinse the tanks after every use. Replace the filter if suction weakens. A pet accident that has been dried for days needs a longer dwell time with the solution before extraction, and a second pass with clear water to rinse out residue that would otherwise attract fresh dirt. For repeat accidents in the same spot, an enzyme-based product used after cleaning helps break down the odor at its source.
products.bestFor: Pet households that want steam plus a dedicated solution.

buyingCriteria.explanation: A portable spot cleaner handles stairs, couches, car seats and fresh spills, but it is slow on a whole room because the clean tank is small and the head is narrow. An upright deep cleaner covers a floor faster but is heavy and bulky. If your main need is pet accidents and furniture, a spot cleaner is the right tool. For wall-to-wall carpet, choose an upright.

Hot water dissolves grease and dried food better than cold, which is why the TREEUP and Uwant offer steam at 212 degrees Fahrenheit and the MUJERBAY heats to 140. Heat can set certain stains, such as blood and some dyes, so test a hidden area first. Steam can also damage delicate fabrics and finished wood. Cold water remains the safest choice for unknown materials.

A larger clean tank, like the Starrybot's 60 ounces, means fewer refills, while a larger dirty tank, like the Rosewill's 53.6 ounces, means fewer trips to empty. The dirty tank fills faster on heavily soiled jobs, so a small one limits you. Tanks also add weight when full, so think about stairs. Check that both tanks are easy to remove and rinse. A wide-mouth tank with a handle is far easier to clean than a narrow one, and a clear tank lets you see when the dirty water is full without guessing. Tanks that click firmly into place also leak less, which protects both the machine and the carpet.

KPa figures such as 18 and 17 are brand claims with no common test, so they are not directly comparable between makers. A machine with a clog-free hose and a good seal will outperform a higher claimed number with a leak. Look at the motor wattage when listed, like the Rosewill's 550W, and at the tool design. Judge by how dry the fabric feels after a pass.

The HAPOW lists a 13.1 foot cord and a 4.9 foot hose, which makes stairs and cars easier. A short cord forces extension cords, and a short hose means moving the base. Measure the longest distance you need, such as from an outlet to the far corner of a car. Reach is a daily convenience.

Use a cleaning solution made for extractors, since ordinary detergent foams and clogs the machine. Drying depends on how much water you leave behind, so do a dry pass with suction only after cleaning. Open windows or run a fan to speed drying. Damp fabric left for days can grow mildew.

howWeEvaluated.title: Heat and cleaning modes
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared steam, hot and cold water options. The TREEUP's four modes and the Uwant's three scored highest for flexibility, and the MUJERBAY scored for gentler heat.

howWeEvaluated.title: Tank layout
howWeEvaluated.description: Clean and dirty tank sizes were weighed against typical jobs. The Starrybot's 60 ounce clean tank and the Rosewill's 53.6 ounce dirty tank stood out.

howWeEvaluated.title: Reach and tools
howWeEvaluated.description: Cord, hose and tool sets were compared. The HAPOW's 13.1 foot cord and the TREEUP's brush set scored for convenience.

howWeEvaluated.title: Suction claims
howWeEvaluated.description: KPa figures were treated as claims and not measurements. Motor wattage, where stated, earned extra credit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fit at the cap
howWeEvaluated.description: Every item is at or under the cap on its live listing. We favored heat and tank design over larger suction numbers.

cards.label: Heated (TREEUP, Uwant, MUJERBAY)
cards.text: Hot water and steam lift grease and speed drying, but heat can set some stains and damage delicate fabrics.

cards.label: Cold-water (Starrybot, HAPOW, Rosewill)
cards.text: Safer for unknown fabrics and simpler, but weaker on grease.

howToChoose.note: Choose heat for kitchen and dining areas, and cold water for unknown or delicate materials.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A pet-formulated solution, a hand tool for corners and heat for stubborn residue. A large dirty tank helps with repeated accidents.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Uwant and Starrybot target pet stains directly, and the TREEUP handles greasy residue.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You clean whole rooms or need heated drying. Upright deep cleaners with brush rolls and heated drying cost more and cover a floor much faster.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You clean a few spots a month, in which case a basic spot cleaner is plenty.

maintenance.why: Dirty water sours within a day. Rinse and leave the tanks open to dry.
Hair and fibers clog the brush and hose. Pull them out and rinse.
A clogged filter cuts suction. Rinse it and let it dry fully.
Scale weakens steam output. Use a vinegar rinse if the manual allows.
Closed damp tanks grow mold and odor.

faq.q: Can a portable cleaner do a whole room?
faq.a: It can, but slowly, because the clean tank is small and the head is narrow. An upright deep cleaner is the right tool for a room.
It buys a portable spot cleaner with large tanks, and in some cases heat or steam. The cap reflects listing prices when this guide was updated.

faq.q: Is steam safe on all carpets?
faq.a: No. Steam can set some stains and damage delicate fibers, so test a hidden patch first and check the care label.

faq.q: How long do these machines last?
faq.a: Three to five years with regular rinsing. Pumps, hoses and filters are the wear points.

faq.q: How long does carpet take to dry?
faq.a: Several hours, depending on how much water you used and the airflow. A dry suction pass and a fan help.
